facts: Haakon brought up his recent encounter with the FBI, and by his account my face darkened at once.
I said, "Let's go outside." Hoke took it, I think, to mean I believed the house was wiretapped.
We walked into the back garden, to a wooded corner of the property, and started pacing.
As we paced, Haakon gave me a detailed account of his interrogation.
I was badly shaken. By his later telling, I asked him endless questions.
He told me he had been reluctant to tell the FBI about his conversation with Eltenton.
I reassured him that he had done the right thing.
I said, "I had to report that conversation, you know."
He said, "Yes," though by his own account he wondered whether it had really been necessary.
Haakon asked, "But what about those alleged approaches to three scientists, and the supposed repeated attempts to get secret information?"
By his account, I gave no reply.
I kept trying to reconstruct what I had told Pash, and I got more and more agitated. Hoke thought I seemed extremely nervous and tense.
Kitty called out, "Darling, the guests are arriving, and I think you'd better come in now." I told her abruptly I'd be in in a minute, and kept pacing, and had Hoke repeat his story.

Minutes later she came out a second time and said I really must come now. I answered curtly, she persisted, and I let loose a flood of foul language at her, calling her vile names and telling her to mind her goddamn business and get the hell out.
Hoke said afterward he had never seen me behave like that. Even then I didn't want to end the conversation, and I gave him no hint of what was bothering me.
